fixes.explanation: True. David says he said in alarm, “I am cut off from Your sight!” Then, “But You heard my plea for mercy when I called to You for help.” (Psalm 31:22) He said it in alarm, and the LORD heard him anyway. Alarm can do a lot of talking, friend.

David never calls the LORD a river in this verse. He says, “For You are my rock and my fortress…” (Psalm 31:3) A river keeps moving, while a rock and a fortress stay put. Those are the two pictures David gives.

David had mighty men (2 Samuel 23:8), but they aren't in this verse. He says, “You free me from the net laid out for me, for You are my refuge.” (Psalm 31:4) The One he credits is the LORD. I think David knew exactly where to look when the net came out.

No baby shower in this verse, friend. David says, “You have redeemed me, O LORD, God of truth.” (Psalm 31:5) Redeemed is the word he uses for what the LORD has done. He says it right as he puts his spirit into the LORD's hands.

A withered tree is a good picture, but it isn't David's. He says, “I am like a broken vessel.” (Psalm 31:12) A vessel is something you carry or pour from, and David compares himself to a broken one. I think he feels cracked all the way through.
David is king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), so crown is a fair guess. But he says, “My times are in Your hands…” (Psalm 31:15) That's his times, not his crown. The hat stays out of this one.
To be silenced. David says, “May lying lips be silenced…” (Psalm 31:18) These are lips that speak with arrogance against the righteous, full of pride and contempt. I think this one hurts.

Clever is tempting, baker. But David says, “The LORD preserves the faithful, but fully repays the arrogant.” (Psalm 31:23) I once got clever and skipped the recipe, and that batch came out flat. The faithful are the ones David names.

No tiptoeing in this last line, baker. Quiet and patient aren't the words David picks. He ends with, “Be strong and courageous, all you who hope in the LORD.” (Psalm 31:24) After a whole psalm of enemies and sorrow, he sends out a call to strength and courage.

Wise and humble are good words, but David doesn't use them here. He ends with, “Be strong and courageous, all you who hope in the LORD.” (Psalm 31:24) Those are big words for a last line, and they're for everyone who hopes in the LORD. Hearing them, I stand a little taller on my gold base.
